speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the skin lesions for me, specifically when they first appeared and whether they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions umbilicated with a central dimple, and have they spread to other parts of the body? I need to know if there is any associated fever or malaise.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of pearly, umbilicated papules with a history of daycare exposure is classic for Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
